items.headline: Vulnerability in Oracle OpenJDK (Java4Shell) Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
items.summary: On November 17, 2026, Oracle announced the availability of fixes for a vulnerability in OpenJDK that could lead to remote code execution identified by CVE-2026-114938. The vulnerability affects OpenJDK Java 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 platforms when processing Base64 encoded content. For more information, see the Oracle Critical Security Patch Update Advisory - November 2026 and the OpenJDK Vulnerability Advisory: 2026/11/17 . For additional information, see the Talos blog post: Talos Threat Advisory CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK JAVA This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cl
lines: Oracle announced fixes on November 17, 2026 for CVE-2026-114938, an OpenJDK vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.
The flaw affects OpenJDK Java 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 platforms when processing Base64 encoded content.
Cisco's advisory on the issue will be updated as more information becomes available. IT teams running affected Java versions should review the Oracle and Cisco advisories.

items.headline: AWS WAF introduces simplified pricing
items.summary: AWS WAF now offers simplified pricing that follows what you protect instead of how you configure it. Previously, you paid separate charges for each web ACL, rule, rule group subscription, and capacity tier, making every security decision a billing calculation. Now, your bill follows three dimensions: the resources you protect, the traffic AWS WAF inspects, and the level of protection you apply. This makes the cost-benefit trade-off easy to understand, and adding or changing rules no longer changes your rate. The new model makes protection costs predictable before you deploy. Each web ACL now includes up to 2,500 WCU at no extra charge, up from 1,500, and you can add rules such as Bot Control
lines: AWS WAF now offers simplified pricing based on the resources protected, the traffic AWS WAF inspects, and the level of protection applied.
Each web ACL now includes up to 2,500 WCU at no extra charge, up from 1,500.
Adding or changing rules no longer changes the rate, which makes protection costs more predictable before deployment.

items.headline: AWS WAF announces automated discovery and protection for LLM, MCP, and A2A endpoints using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
items.summary: Automated AI endpoint discovery and protection are now generally available, enabling you to discover language model (LLM), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancers, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS Organization and protect them using AWS WAF. Discovery is available through the new API Gateway API Portal, which recognizes the AI endpoints among the APIs it discovers automatically from traffic logs and service configuration records, with no agents to deploy or logs to forward. An undocumented, public-facing MCP server appears as a shadow API. For unprotected AI endpoints, customers can enable protection using WAF.
lines: Automated AI endpoint discovery and protection are now generally available in AWS WAF.
Discovery covers LLM, MCP, and A2A endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancers, and Amazon CloudFront across an AWS Organization.
Discovery requires no agents to deploy or logs to forward. Unprotected AI endpoints can be protected with WAF, and undocumented public MCP servers appear as shadow APIs.

items.headline: Amazon Connect Customer launches the ability to force logout agents directly from the analytics dashboard
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer now allows supervisors to force logout agents directly from the real-time analytics dashboard, eliminating the need to manually contact agents to end their sessions. Force logout ends all active agent sessions and records the logout event in the Login/Logout report, so agent timecards stay complete. For example, a supervisor identifies an agent who left their workstation without logging out after a shift, and force logs them out from the dashboard, preventing idle time from accruing on the agent's timecard. items.headline: Amazon CloudFront is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
items.summary: Amazon CloudFront is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud. Organizations with strict EU sovereignty requirements can now deliver websites, applications, and APIs with the performance, security, and scale of CloudFront, all within the EU. Until now, customers had to build and run their own delivery and TLS termination infrastructure to keep traffic and data inside the EU. With CloudFront in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud, content delivery, TLS termination, logs, and customer configuration stay within the European Sovereign Cloud boundary. The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is physically and logically separate from other AWS Regions, and only EU-resident personnel operate it. This
lines: Amazon CloudFront is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud.
Content delivery, TLS termination, logs, and customer configuration stay within the European Sovereign Cloud boundary.

The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is physically and logically separate from other AWS Regions, and only EU-resident personnel operate it. Organizations with strict EU sovereignty requirements can avoid building their own delivery infrastructure.

items.headline: Amazon EC2 X8i instances are now available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region
items.summary: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) X8i instances are available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region. items.headline: AWS Sign-In introduces configurable Sign-in duration of up to 90 days
items.summary: AWS Sign-In now enables developers and AI agents to stay authenticated for up to 90 days without frequent sign-ins or consent prompts. With this launch, administrators can configure Sign-in duration , which controls how long an OAuth Sign-in session remains active, for individual IAM users and roles. This capability reduces authentication interruptions for long-running workflows and provides a more secure alternative to static access keys by using short-lived, renewable credentials. Existing session duration limits remain unchanged unless administrators explicitly configure longer durations. Sign-In Duration supports AWS CLI (aws login), AWS MCP Server, and other OAuth-enabled applications.
lines: AWS Sign-In now lets developers and AI agents stay authenticated for up to 90 days without frequent sign-ins or consent prompts.
Administrators can configure Sign-in duration for individual IAM users and roles, and it supports AWS CLI (aws login), AWS MCP Server, and other OAuth-enabled applications.
Existing session duration limits remain unchanged unless administrators explicitly configure longer durations.

"It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches," OpenAI said in a post on X. lines: Reported by The Hacker News: OpenAI and Cisco launched Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime that lets AI agents defend systems without downtime.

The critical vulnerabilities are listed below - CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in N-able MailAssure's LDAP
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: CISA added two flaws affecting N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Monday, citing evidence of active exploitation.
